_about: Hand-researched CEO notes for STM and the shortlisted stocks, compiled 2026-11-27 from the linked public sources (paraphrased; quotes as reported by those sources). Re-check before relying on them.

STM.name: Jean-Marc Chery
approach: Continuity and execution discipline: the board reappointed him for one more year (Oct 2026) citing steady strategy and execution.
how: Operations-first leader: joined Thomson Semiconducteurs (now ST) in 1986, ran product planning and manufacturing, then was COO for technology and manufacturing from 2014.
Answers to state shareholders: France and Italy own 27.5%; Italy's economy minister has publicly criticised him.

LULU.name: Heidi O'Neill
approach: Product-led growth: faster product breakthroughs, stronger cultural relevance, growth outside North America.
how: 25+ years at Nike, most recently president of consumer, product and brand.
Started with a deep review of strategy and the current action plan, per the interim CEO.

quotes.text: My job will be to build on that foundation -- to accelerate product breakthroughs, deepen the brand's cultural relevance, and unlock growth in markets around the world.

GL.name: Frank Svoboda & Matt Darden (co-CEOs)
approach: Serve the lower-middle and middle-income market with simple protection products.
Grow by adding exclusive agents: target 28,000+ agents and $1.4B annual sales by 2030.
how: Split roles: Svoboda was CFO, Darden was chief strategy officer.
Recruits mostly people with no insurance background; middle-manager pay rewards recruiting and keeping new agents.

quotes.text: Long-term growth is dependent on agent count growth.
quotes.source: Globe Life Q3 2025 earnings call (paraphrase of Darden)

SYF.name: Brian Doubles
approach: Diversify revenue beyond store cards: e-commerce and health-care partnerships, a 2% cash-back card.
how: Culture and trust first: declined a return-to-office mandate and keeps hybrid work.
Grows through retail partnerships and acquisitions.

sources.label: American Banker: new CEO bets on health care, e-commerce

CTSH.name: Ravi Kumar S
approach: Turn Cognizant from systems integrator into an "AI builder" that closes the gap between AI spending and business value.
how: Tracks revenue and margin per person as the scorecard.
Hires beyond STEM, including liberal-arts graduates; uses AI to write a growing share of code.
Buys only companies that fit the platforms-and-operations thesis.

quotes.text: AI is an amplifier of human potential. It's not a displacement strategy.

DECK.name: Stefano Caroti
approach: Push HOKA and UGG toward fashion-lifestyle customers and grow faster outside the US.
Sustainable, profitable growth over chasing volume.
how: Company insider since 2015 (omnichannel, then chief commercial officer and interim HOKA president).
Adjusts execution when needed, e.g. wider spacing between major product launches.

sources.label: Retail Dive: Deckers names Caroti CEO

ACGL.name: Nicolas Papadopoulo
approach: Cycle management: write more when prices are high, shrink when returns fall below target.
Deploy capital only into business that clears return thresholds.
how: Uses third-party capital to manage net exposure.
Keeps Arch's long-standing underwriting-cycle framework (dating back to 1985).

quotes.text: We will not chase growth for the sake of growth.
We are reducing participation where returns no longer meet our objectives.
